description: I am Aaditya Sangroula. I am looking for teammates who can help and cooperate with building something unique and totally out of the box even though it seems senseless at the initial phases. We'll surely turn it into something sensible. That's the motive of science, to find patterns in what seems random. We also find sense in things what look senseless.
summary:
Moonhunters is a 3D moon exploration game where you play as an astronaut on a mission in the year 2042.

You land near a giant moon crater and set out to explore. You can hop around in low gravity on foot or hop into a moon buggy to drive across the rugged lunar surface. Along the way, you collect interesting rock samples, scan minerals, set up communication antennas, and explore abandoned lunar structures. You also have to keep an eye on your oxygen and stamina so you don't run out while you're away from base.

You can play through guided story missions, wander freely in open-world mode, or team up with friends online. It's built as a smooth, fast PC desktop app designed to run at high frame rates with cool features like radar scanning, dynamic sun shadows, and cinematic intros.
details:
At its heart, Moonhunters is a game about what it would actually feel like to stand on the Moon. When you start, you're an astronaut stepping out of your lander onto a huge, quiet lunar landscape. You can hop around in the floaty, low gravity or hop into a moon buggy and go cruising across giant craters. Along the way, you hunt down interesting moon rocks, drill for samples, set up radio towers, and keep an eye on your oxygen meter so you don't wander off too far and get stranded. We built this because space science can sometimes feel pretty dry in books, and we wanted to turn that feeling of real discovery into something hands-on and exciting that anyone can just pick up and enjoy. We built the whole thing using web technologies—mostly JavaScript and Three.js for the 3D world, terrain, and physics—and then wrapped it into a proper Windows desktop app with Electron so you can just launch it and play offline with zero setup. We tried to get creative with the little details that make it feel alive: dust kicking up under your boots, the way the sun casts long, harsh shadows across the dust, the crackle of mission control over your helmet radio, and the freedom to jump in and out of your rover whenever you want. Above all, we wanted the game to feel incredibly smooth and responsive. We spent a lot of time tuning performance so it runs without any jitter or lag, keeping the controls simple and fun while still honoring real lunar science.

We have used MIT open source project for the base of our project:https://winchxyz.github.io/moon-rover/
